disposition_reason: Dietary iron intake estimates (haem and non-haem) and serum ferritin associations in 270 young women; no food concentration measurements.
disposition_locator: Table 2 p. 6; Table 3 p. 7; Results p. 5

study.method: Semi-quantitative FFQ (DQES v2); serum ferritin by Roche immunoassay with inflammation correction
study.qa: Accredited diagnostic laboratory for blood analytes

regulatory_or_exposure: Energy-adjusted mean intake (n = 270): total iron 12.7 ± 2.6 mg/day; haem iron 2.0 ± 0.9 mg/day; non-haem iron 10.7 ± 2.7 mg/day (Table 2)
Iron deficiency 26.3% (ferritin < 20 ug/L) and iron deficiency anemia 5.9% (Hb < 120 g/L) (Results p. 5)
Serum ferritin model: haem iron beta 0.128 (p = 0.009), non-haem iron beta 0.037 (p = 0.028); adjusted R squared 0.058 (Table 3)
non_numeric_findings: Haem iron was a stronger predictor of ferritin than non-haem iron.
High dietary restraint was associated with lower energy intake.
Original data collection funded by Meat and Livestock Australia.
